channel.title: Hrshop — Latest articles
channel.description: A calm field guide to working together. Independent editorial about everyday workplace practices.

item.title: Beginning Again: On Returning to Work After a Break
item.author: editor@hrshop.com (Eleanor Whitcombe)
item.description: Returning to work after months or years away is a small brave act. A patient essay for anyone starting again, and a set of small honest suggestions for a first four weeks back at a desk.

item.title: Rest Is Part of Working: On Breaks, Pauses, and Focus
item.author: editor@hrshop.com (Eleanor Whitcombe)
item.description: Rest is not the pause between work and life — it is part of the work itself. A patient look at breaks, pauses, holidays and the small honest work of stopping so you can start again.

item.title: Understanding Your Own Working Week
item.author: editor@hrshop.com (Marcus Tremlett)
item.description: Your working week is different from everyone else's. A calm guide to noticing your own patterns — your good hours, your meeting appetite, your quiet days — and working with them rather than against them.

item.title: An Introduction to Async Communication
item.author: editor@hrshop.com (Marcus Tremlett)
item.description: Async communication is not the absence of meetings; it is a craft of writing well when the reply comes later. A patient introduction for teams that want fewer meetings and clearer messages.

item.title: How to Say No, Kindly, at Work
item.author: editor@hrshop.com (Eleanor Whitcombe)
item.description: Saying no at work is a small kindness done honestly. A patient guide to declining requests, deferring tasks and setting limits without damaging the relationship on the other side.

item.title: The Twelve Small Habits of Steady Team Work
item.author: editor@hrshop.com (Eleanor Whitcombe)
item.description: Twelve small habits — none dramatic on their own — that quietly turn a team from a group of individuals into a working team. Saying good morning, closing the loop, keeping promises small.

item.title: How to Build a Weeknight Wind-Down for Remote Teams
item.author: editor@hrshop.com (Marcus Tremlett)
item.description: A remote team without an end-of-day ritual quietly works too long. A patient guide to building a weeknight wind-down that respects working hours and gives the day a genuine close.

item.title: Field Notes on Small Team Meetings
item.author: editor@hrshop.com (Marcus Tremlett)
item.description: A patient set of notes on the small team meeting — the sort with six or eight people around a table or a call — and the small honest habits that make it feel worth the half hour.

item.title: How to Give Feedback That Feels Real
item.author: editor@hrshop.com (Eleanor Whitcombe)
item.description: Feedback that lands well is a small kindness. A calm guide to giving feedback that is specific, timely and honest — and to receiving it without either flinching or performing agreement.

item.title: The Method of a Weekly One-to-One, Explained Gently
item.author: editor@hrshop.com (Eleanor Whitcombe)
item.description: A patient walk through the weekly one-to-one — what belongs in it, what does not, and how a thirty-minute conversation every week quietly changes a working relationship.

item.title: Onboarding, Slowly
item.author: editor@hrshop.com (Eleanor Whitcombe)
item.description: Onboarding is not an event, it is a season. A patient look at the first month of a new job from both sides — what the new person needs, what the team can offer, and how to make a good beginning.

item.title: A Quiet Introduction to Hiring Conversations
item.author: editor@hrshop.com (Eleanor Whitcombe)
item.description: A calm walk through hiring conversations — how to write an honest job description, prepare for an interview, listen properly, and make a decision that respects the person on the other side of the desk.
